task.title: Configuring secure station communication
task.shortdesc: This topic explains how to set up secure Foxs and Https communication for Supervisor and controller stations.

taskbody.context: Follow this procedure for both Foxs and Webs.

step.cmd: Make a secure connection to the station.
Right-click FoxService or WebService under ConfigServices in the Nav tree.
step.stepresult: The Property Sheet opens and click ViewsProperty Sheet.

step.cmd: Confirm that the true check box is selected for Foxs Enabled or Https Enabled.
From the Foxs Cert or Https Cert list, select the appropriate certificate.
step.stepresult:
Each platform/station should have its own unique, signed server certificate. Do not use the same server certificate for more than one platform/station. If you choose to use a different certificate for your FoxService from that used for your WebService, this is where you specify it.
If your network architecture includes a reverse proxy, additional configuration is required to ensure Fox protocol connections function correctly. To enable Fox protocol traversal through a reverse proxy, set the following system property in the system.properties file:org.bouncycastle.jsse.client.assumeOriginalHostName=false. This property instructs the Bouncy Castle JSSE client to include the original host name in the TLS handshake's ClientHello message via the Server Name Indication (SNI) extension.
You should set this property to true whenever a instance - whether it is Workbench or a station, and regardless of the platform (Win32, Linux, or Containerized - connects to another instance through a reverse proxy that uses SNI (Server Name Indication).This setting allows the proxy to correctly identify and present the appropriate certificate to the client. After updating the system.properties file, restart the station for the change to take effect.
